entry.title: 🏆Winner of the ESD Association Outstanding Contributions Award 2026

media:group.media:title: 🏆Winner of the ESD Association Outstanding Contributions Award 2026
media:group.media:description:
The ESD Association has honored Dr. Horst Gieser of #FraunhoferEMFT for his pioneering work on Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) testing. Since 1989 at @TUMuenchen1 and continued at Fraunhofer EMFT in 1994, Dr. Gieser and his team have studied the complex interaction between device and tester and their imperfections.
🤝His commitment to applied science, mutual respect, and collaboration has helped build enduring partnerships across continents.
🙏He extends his heartfelt thanks to his collaborators and friends in industry and academia worldwide, his team, colleagues, and management at Fraunhofer EMFT, and his family. Their support has made this journey of more than three decades possible. And it is still far from over.

entry.title: Sub-micron precision, now live in our lab.

media:group.media:title: Sub-micron precision, now live in our lab.
media:group.media:description:
Our new Femto 2 flip-chip bonder from @finetech-world has joined the process chain at #FraunhoferEMFT, expanding what we can assemble for our partners.
📍 0.3 µm placement accuracy at 3 sigma 🎯 80 nm alignment accuracy
This covers the challenges our partners bring to us most often: ultra-fine-pitch interconnects, high-density packaging, and sensor systems on thin, flexible substrates rather than rigid boards.
System capabilities include:
✅ Components from 30 × 30 µm to 100 × 100 mm ✅ Bonding forces from 0.2 N to 1,000 N ✅ Independent heating up to 450 °C (chip) and 300 °C (substrate) ✅ Ultrasonic bonding and UV curing ✅ Time-pressure and jet dispensing for repeatable volumes ✅ Oxide-free bonding under nitrogen or formic acid in an enclosed process chamber
The system is one part of the equation. The other is our process know-how in foil-based chip integration — from initial feasibility studies to a transferable production process.
👉 Learn more about our capabilities in foil-based chip integration, or get in touch to discuss your application: https://www.emft.fraunhofer.de/en/research-development/flexible-systems/foil-based-chip-integration.html

entry.title: How do you find a defect you can't even see?

media:group.media:title: How do you find a defect you can't even see?
media:group.media:description:
At #FraunhoferEMFT, our failure analysis lab tackles exactly this challenge every day. As chip technologies get more complex — from 🔗 heterointegration to 📦 advanced packaging — finding what's gone wrong inside them gets harder too.
💡 That's why we're developing new failure analysis methods, including the #QuantumDiamondMicroscope (QDM).
💎 Here's the trick: NV centers in diamond can detect magnetic fields with extreme sensitivity. Since every current flow generates a magnetic field, we can use this to "see" current paths inside a chip — without ever touching it optically. This is called Magnetic Current Imaging (MCI), and it lets us locate defects that other methods simply can't find, including ones that produce no heat at all.
✨ Unlike other MCI techniques, QDM works at room temperature, captures all three magnetic field components, and enables quantitative current measurements — a powerful complement to established failure analysis approaches, especially for tricky cases like open circuits and shorts in advanced packaging.
👉 Curious how it works in practice? Learn more about our Quantum Diamond Microscope and failure analysis capabilities: https://www.emft.fraunhofer.de/en/research-development/test-analysis/quantum-diamond-microscope.html

entry.title: Sensorsystem ermöglicht in-situ Bodenanalysen vor Ort

media:group.media:title: Sensorsystem ermöglicht in-situ Bodenanalysen vor Ort
media:group.media:description: Gesunde Böden sind eine Grundlage für eine nachhaltige und gleichzeitig ertragsreiche landwirtschaftliche Nutzung. In situ-Messungen von indikativen Bodenparametern wären daher für Landwirtinnen und Landwirte ein effektives Tool, um die Bewirtschaftung zu optimieren – bisher sind allerdings kaum praktikable Lösungen am Markt verfügbar. Forschende des Fraunhofer EMFT entwickeln im Projekt FAMOSOS gemeinsam mit Partnern ein Messsystem, das Echtzeit-Bodendaten zu Stoffflüssen wie Stickstoff (Ammonium, Nitrat, Lachgas), Feuchtigkeit, pH-Wert und gelöstem Sauerstoff liefert.

entry.title: 💉 What if a drug delivery system could reliably dispense just 0.05 units of insulin?

media:group.media:title: 💉 What if a drug delivery system could reliably dispense just 0.05 units of insulin?
media:group.media:description:
In this video, our colleague Mohammad gives an inside look at the development of MEMS-based silicon piezo micropumps at #FraunhoferEMFT and explains how they are paving the way for the next generation of medical drug delivery systems.
🔬 Highlights: ✔️ Reliable dosing of 100 nanoliters per stroke of U500 insulin (0.05 units per bolus) ✔️ Stable dosing accuracy over a 3-day patch pump cycle ✔️ Silicon micropumps only a few millimeters in size ✔️ Enabling smaller, smarter and more precise wearable drug delivery devices
To further improve reliability, our researchers are developing self-sensing technology that allows the micropump to detect gas bubbles or blockages in real time - an important step toward safer and more robust medical devices.
Watch the video to learn how our researchers are advancing next-generation patch pumps and precision drug delivery.
👉 Learn more about our Piezo Micropumps here: https://www.emft.fraunhofer.de/en/research-development/micropumps/piezo-micropumps.html

entry.title: Every measurement tells a story. The right analytics reveal it.

media:group.media:title: Every measurement tells a story. The right analytics reveal it.
media:group.media:description:
n #semiconductor and #MEMS manufacturing, precision doesn't end with fabrication. It depends on understanding every process step.
At #FraunhoferEMFT, our in-line process analytics provide the insights needed to monitor, optimize and validate manufacturing processes – from research and development to industrial production.
Our analytics capabilities include: 🔍 Optical microscopy & reflectometry for fast process inspection 📏 Profilometry for precise step-height measurements 📐 Wafer thickness & bow measurement for reliable process control 🧪 Surface characterization with TOF-SIMS, AFM, Raman spectroscopy & wetting angle analysis ⚡ Comprehensive analytical methods for CMOS and MEMS technologies Every measurement helps detect deviations early, improve process stability and maximize yield.
🤝 Looking for a partner for process development, in-line analytics or semiconductor manufacturing?
Our experts are happy to discuss your project and find the right solution together. Get in touch – we'd love to hear from you.

entry.title: ♻️ What if electronics could disassemble themselves?

media:group.media:title: ♻️ What if electronics could disassemble themselves?
media:group.media:description:
Every year, millions of tons of electronic waste are generated worldwide, while valuable materials remain locked inside discarded devices. Automating disassembly is one of the key challenges on the path toward a true circular economy.
Our automated PCB handling demonstrator is a step toward that vision. Combining robotics, sensor fusion and AI-powered perception, it enables the precise identification and handling of electronic assemblies.
Looking ahead, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models will allow robots to go beyond predefined routines: understanding instructions, interpreting complex environments and autonomously deciding how to act. These capabilities are essential for future disassembly and recycling processes, where no two products are exactly alike.
🎥 See how intelligent robotics can help make circular electronics a reality.

entry.title: What happens when plasma meets precision? 💡

media:group.media:title: What happens when plasma meets precision? 💡
media:group.media:description:
Structures emerge that are invisible to the naked eye - but essential for the technologies we rely on every day.
In our highly automated 200 mm #CMOS line, advanced plasma etching processes shape dielectrics, metals and silicon with nanometer-level precision. From #sensor technologies and #MEMS to complex semiconductor devices, these processes reveal the structures that make innovation possible.
Behind every breakthrough #chip or #microsystem lies a process that removes exactly what doesn't belong. 💿
Find out more: https://www.emft.fraunhofer.de/en/technologies-microelectronics-microsystem-technology/cmos-line.html
